kicker: Capital goods · order books vs sales, Q2 FY27
title: Order books are filling faster than factories ship
dek: Dee Development's order book is up 94% and HLE Glascoat's 51%, yet their Q2 sales grew 9% and fell 1%. At five of seven equipment makers, sales grew at under half the pace of the order book.

chart.title: Order book growth, 30 Sep 2026 vs a year earlier
chart.sub: label adds Q2 FY27 sales growth YoY · Elecon = gear division

legend.c: Sales growing at under half the book's pace
legend.a: Sales growing faster than the book

stats.label: Dee's October execution
stats.note: Against roughly ₹150 cr a month needed to reach its ₹1,500 cr FY27 revenue goal.

stats.label: HLE's order-to-revenue lag
stats.note: Builds take 4–7 months and revenue is booked only on dispatch; book ₹1,087 cr.

stats.label: TARIL's standalone EBITDA margin
stats.note: From 8.8% a year ago, as sales (+66%) caught up with its ₹7,237 cr book.

read: Winning orders is no longer the constraint for these makers; H2 FY27 is the execution test, and slipping dispatches would push revenue into FY28.
sources: Vantage analysis of Q2 FY27 results filed on BSE and Q2 FY27 earnings calls; Vantage sector intel, 21 Nov 2026
notes: Order book growth is each company's stated change in closing order book at 30 Sep 2026 against 30 Sep 2025 (TARIL: standalone unexecuted book; Elecon: gear division open orders; GMM Pfaudler: consolidated backlog; Lohia: as read back on its call). Sales growth is Q2 FY27 revenue from operations against Q2 FY26 from filed consolidated results, except Lohia (from its call; no year-ago filing on the desk) and Elecon (gear division revenue per its call). A year-on-year order book change set against one quarter's sales shows direction, not a precise book-to-bill ratio. Dee's book includes a GE letter of intent of about $40 mn not yet converted to a purchase order; HLE's includes a Fehmarnbelt cladding order of about ₹210–220 cr. Dee's ₹150 cr monthly run-rate is from its call, against H1 FY27 revenue of ₹587 cr.
